title: Teaching in the schools from 1934 with Professor Turo
summary: He explains that after returning in 1932 he began teaching school bands with Professor Turo and his father.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: How long have you been teaching music now too?

Well I've been, I've been in this, let's say about, 1934, since 1934, 33 or 34. See when I came back from St. Louis, there was no work. Depression then. Depression, see I came back in 32. And I believe my, yeah my daddy was here. They went, we were, he was a fellow named Professor Turo. He was a fine musician. I don't know if anybody ever mentioned him, he's a fine musician around here. And through him and my, he and my daddy, while I got to work in the school, through this private school, see. And we had access to all the public schools. Little political stuff, you see, they did. And then I used to go and teach the different school bands in the afternoons. Because there's a lawyer, you can't teach in there until after, after three o'clock, you see. Yeah, for private people, you know. And we used to go in, I'd be at three o'clock, and at three to five, he did too. So we had access to all the schools. Your father taught them in the schools? He did, yeah, that's right. And, well, it didn't look like much, but do you know, you're parling nickels and dimes up, it sort of mounted something.
